title: Analysis: India’s power-sector emissions flat for two years due to clean-energy surge - Carbon Brief
gist: India's record clean-energy build-out — 77GW of solar in two years — absorbed the entire 63TWh rise in electricity demand from H1 2024 to H1 2026, holding power-sector CO2 flat and delivering the first two-year period in more than 50 years with no coal-power growth. But total emissions still rose 3.7% year-on-year in H1 2026 because steel and cement emissions grew 8% and now make up 23% of India's CO2, and continued coal-gasification, coking-coal and coal-mining investment threatens decades of lock-in.

themes.theme: Power-sector emissions plateau and the coal-growth break

insights.claim: CO2 emissions from India's power sector were the same in the first half of 2026 as two years earlier, after a 2.2% decline in H1 2025 was reversed by a 2.3% rise in H1 2026.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: The world's fastest-growing large power market has decoupled generation growth from emissions for two straight years.
insights.quote: India’s power-sector emissions flatlined at 2024 levels, after a 2.2% decline in the first half of 2025 and a 2.3% rise in the same period this year.

insights.claim: This is the first time in more than 50 years that India has seen no growth in coal power over a two-year period while electricity demand was still rising.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A half-century structural relationship between Indian demand growth and coal burn has broken, with direct implications for seaborne thermal coal demand.
insights.quote: This is the first time in more than 50 years that there has been no growth in India’s coal power over a two-year period, even as electricity demand grew overall.

insights.claim: Despite the flat power sector and falling oil and gas use, India's total emissions still grew 3.7% year-on-year in the first half of 2026 because of increases from steel, cement and other sectors.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Power-sector decarbonisation alone no longer determines India's emissions trajectory; industry is now the swing factor.
insights.quote: the new six-monthly analysis for Carbon Brief shows that India’s emissions grew by 3.7% year-on-year in the first half of 2026, due to increases from steel, cement and other sectors

themes.theme: Clean-energy build-out absorbs all demand growth

insights.claim: From the first half of 2024 to the first half of 2026, India's total power generation rose 7%, or 63TWh, and that entire additional requirement was met by clean energy.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Marginal electricity demand in India is now being served by zero-carbon supply, capping thermal fuel burn at existing levels.
insights.quote: The additional power requirement of 63TWh was met entirely by clean energy.

insights.claim: India added 77GW of new solar capacity, 11GW of wind, 5GW of hydro and 0.6GW of nuclear over the two-year period, with solar alone helping meet 60% of the rise in electricity demand.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Solar module and inverter demand from India is running at a scale that sets global manufacturing utilisation.
insights.quote: Over the past two years, India added 77GW of new solar capacity, 11GW of wind, 5GW of hydro and 0.6GW of nuclear capacity.

insights.claim: Although solar dominates headline growth, non-solar clean sources collectively still contributed 40% of the overall increase in India's generation.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A solar-only reading of India's transition understates the role of wind, hydro and nuclear in firming the system.
insights.quote: Solar power continues to dominate clean-energy growth, but, collectively, the other non-fossil sources still contributed 40% of the overall increase in generation.

insights.claim: Added power generation from new clean capacity has stayed above average demand growth for the past 18 months, implying the pipeline is more than sufficient to sustain the flat-emissions trend.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Forward-looking capacity data, not just backward emissions data, points to continued fossil stagnation in Indian power.
insights.quote: new investments are more than sufficient to maintain this trend, as added power generation from new clean power capacity has stayed above average demand growth for the past 18 months

insights.claim: For scale comparison, China's combined nuclear, wind and solar output increased by 485TWh in 2025 alone, roughly seven times India's two-year clean-generation addition.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: India's record build-out is still an order of magnitude smaller than China's, tempering claims that India is the decisive global swing factor.
insights.quote: (For comparison, China’s nuclear, wind and solar output increased by 485TWh in 2025.)

insights.claim: An El Nino in 2026 delayed the monsoon and intensified heatwaves, driving up cooling demand and inflating electricity demand growth.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Part of 2026's demand growth is weather-driven and could mean-revert, flattering or flattening next year's comparisons.
insights.quote: One factor in electricity demand growth in 2026 is the El Niño, which delayed the monsoon and intensified heatwaves, driving up cooling demand.

themes.theme: State-level divergence in the clean-power shift

insights.claim: Gujarat recorded both the largest reduction in fossil-fuel generation and the largest expansion in clean power of any Indian state between H1 2024 and H1 2026.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Identifies the single state where the coal-to-clean substitution is most advanced, a template and a demand signal for developers.
insights.quote: Gujarat saw both the largest reduction in fossil-fuel generation and the largest expansion in clean power
insights.locator: Which states led the clean-power shift?

insights.claim: Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu recorded the largest increases in clean-power generation after Gujarat and also cut their fossil-fuel generation.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Three states are carrying most of India's coal displacement, concentrating transmission and curtailment risk there.
insights.quote: the largest increases in clean-power generation were seen in Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu, which also saw reductions in power generation from fossil fuels
insights.locator: Which states led the clean-power shift?

insights.claim: Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh grew clean power faster than their own demand but exported much of the increase, so their local fossil generation rose even as they helped hold national coal burn stable.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Export-oriented renewable states bear local fossil costs while delivering national benefits, a tension for state-level incentives.
insights.quote: However, they exported much of the increase and consequently saw local increases in power generation from fossil fuels.
insights.locator: Which states led the clean-power shift?

themes.theme: Oil and gas demand decline and the Hormuz shock

insights.claim: India's oil consumption fell 1.3% year-on-year in the first half of 2026, accelerating from a 0.7% decline in the same period a year earlier, and oil and gas CO2 emissions fell 7% year-on-year.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: The market long treated as global oil demand's growth engine is now shrinking two years running.
insights.quote: India’s oil consumption continued to fall during the first half of 2026, dropping 1.3% year-on-year, a slight acceleration from the 0.7% reduction in the same period last year.
insights.locator: Fall in oil and gas consumption continues

insights.claim: India's oil and gas consumption has flatlined for two years after half a century of continuous growth interrupted only briefly by Covid-19.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A 50-year structural growth trend in a top-three oil importer has stalled, with direct consequences for crude demand forecasts.
insights.quote: India’s consumption has been flatlining for the past two years, after half a century of continuous growth that was only briefly interrupted by Covid-19

insights.claim: The headline oil decline masks growth in transport fuels: diesel consumption growth accelerated from 1.8% to 4.1% and petrol returned to 6.9% growth after zero growth a year earlier.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Road-fuel demand is still robust; the decline is driven by LPG, petcoke and industrial feedstocks, a very different investment read.
insights.quote: While diesel and petrol consumption continued to grow, oil consumption was pulled down overall by declines in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), petcoke (a solid derivative of oil used in the cement industry) and industrial feedstocks.
insights.locator: Fall in oil and gas consumption continues

insights.claim: India hit its 20% ethanol blending target five years ahead of schedule in 2025-26, and the increase in blending shaved a full percentage point off petrol consumption growth.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Biofuel policy is quietly destroying roughly a point of Indian gasoline demand growth per year, despite public opposition.
insights.quote: India achieved its 20% ethanol blending target five years ahead of schedule in 2025-26.
insights.locator: Fall in oil and gas consumption continues

insights.claim: The Hormuz crisis disrupted international aviation through temporary airspace closures and cancellations to Middle Eastern destinations, and elevated fuel prices slowed India's aviation fuel demand growth from 5% to 2%.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A geopolitical chokepoint event is visible directly in Indian jet-fuel volumes and airline operating costs.
insights.quote: The slowdown coincided with the strait of Hormuz and wider crisis, which disrupted international aviation through temporary airspace closures and flight cancellations to several Middle Eastern destinations.
insights.locator: Fall in oil and gas consumption continues

insights.claim: LPG consumption in India contracted 7% after 5.7% growth a year earlier, amid disruptions in global LPG markets following the Hormuz crisis.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: LPG is the single biggest swing factor in India's oil decline and is supply-driven, not a structural efficiency gain.
insights.quote: LPG consumption contracted by 7%, after 5.7% growth in the same period last year, amid disruptions in global LPG markets following the Hormuz crisis.
insights.locator: Fall in oil and gas consumption continues

insights.claim: Petcoke consumption fell 9.9%, more than reversing a 9.3% increase the previous year, because rising petcoke prices pushed cement manufacturers to switch to coal.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: An oil-product demand decline that is really a fuel-switch into coal — lower oil volumes, no emissions benefit.
insights.quote: Rising petcoke prices encouraged cement manufacturers to switch to coal.
insights.locator: Fall in oil and gas consumption continues

insights.claim: Naphtha demand contracted as import prices nearly doubled and domestic prices rose around 60%, prompting petrochemical manufacturers to cut operating rates.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Indian petrochemical margins and run rates are being squeezed by feedstock price shock, a direct read for regional chemical spreads.
insights.quote: Naphtha demand contracted as import prices nearly doubled and domestic prices increased by around 60%, prompting petrochemical manufacturers to reduce operating rates
insights.locator: Fall in oil and gas consumption continues

insights.claim: Delhi launched an EV policy targeting two-wheelers, three-wheelers, commercial vehicles and high-mileage segments alongside expanded charging infrastructure, with higher EV adoption set to moderate emissions growth from petrol.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: High-mileage two- and three-wheeler electrification is the fastest lever on Indian gasoline demand, and policy is now targeting it explicitly.
insights.quote: an EV policy was launched to accelerate electrification of the vehicle fleet, with a particular focus on two-wheelers, three-wheelers (auto rickshaws), commercial vehicles and high-mileage segments
insights.locator: Fall in oil and gas consumption continues

insights.claim: Clean-energy expansion cut India's use of imported coal for power by 38% and imported gas by 35%, reducing exposure to the Hormuz shock and improving the trade balance.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Renewables are functioning as an energy-security and balance-of-payments hedge, which is the argument most likely to sustain policy support.
insights.quote: with the use of imported coal falling 38% and the use of gas by 35%, supporting the energy security aims of the government and reducing exposure to the Hormuz shock

insights.claim: High prices and fuel shortages from the Hormuz crisis led Indian state governments to reverse bans on dirtier fuels such as fuel oil, kerosene and coal in industry and commercial establishments.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Energy-price shocks erode environmental regulation quickly, showing how fragile fuel-quality rules are under stress.
insights.quote: high prices and fuel shortages due to the Hormuz crisis led state governments to reverse their orders banning the use of dirtier fuels such as fuel oil, kerosene and coal in industries and commercial establishments

themes.theme: Heavy industry as the new emissions engine

insights.claim: Steel and cement emissions grew 8% year-on-year in the first half of 2026 and reached a 23% share of India's total CO2.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Nearly a quarter of India's carbon now comes from two hard-to-abate industries growing at 8% a year.
insights.quote: Steel and cement emissions grew by 8% year-on-year, reaching a 23% share of India’s total CO2 in the first half of 2026.

insights.claim: Steel and cement output grew 8% and 9% respectively in H1 2026 despite rising input prices and weakening profitability, supported partly by increased real-estate investment especially in the second quarter.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Indian industrial volume growth is being pulled by property, so a real-estate slowdown would be the main brake on emissions.
insights.quote: Steel and cement output in India grew by 8% and 9%, respectively, year-on-year in the first half of 2026, despite rising input prices and weakening profitability.
insights.locator: Rapid emission growth from heavy industry continues

insights.claim: Margins of Indian steel and cement manufacturers stayed under pressure from elevated raw-material costs, particularly imported coking coal, and higher freight costs stemming from the Hormuz crisis.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Input-cost inflation from a shipping chokepoint is squeezing Indian heavy-industry earnings directly.
insights.quote: profit margins of Indian steel and cement manufacturers remained under pressure for much of the period due to elevated raw material costs – particularly imported coking coal – and higher freight costs
insights.locator: Rapid emission growth from heavy industry continues

insights.claim: Indian cement prices are expected to rise to levels last seen in the 2021-22 financial year, when Russia's cut in gas exports to Europe drove a sharp increase in fossil-fuel prices.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Cement price inflation back to an energy-crisis peak could dampen construction volumes and thus industrial emissions growth.
insights.quote: Cement prices are expected to rise to levels last seen in the 2021-22 financial year
insights.locator: Rapid emission growth from heavy industry continues

insights.claim: Coal consumption outside the steel, cement and power sectors accelerated to 14% growth in H1 2026 from 3% a year earlier, as the LPG shortage prompted a shift to coal.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: An LPG supply shock is pushing diffuse industrial and commercial users back onto coal, an emissions channel that policy is not tracking.
insights.quote: coal-consumption growth accelerated to 14% in the first half of 2026, up from 3% last year, as the LPG shortage prompted a shift to coal
insights.locator: Rapid emission growth from heavy industry continues

insights.claim: The Indian government officially authorised the hospitality industry to use coal, refuse-derived fuel pellets, biomass and kerosene for one month during the gas shortage, and states including Delhi NCR, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Maharashtra allowed industries to use alternative fuels temporarily.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that gas scarcity forces regulators to unwind clean-fuel mandates at short notice.
insights.quote: The government officially authorised the hospitality industry to use coal, refuse-derived fuel pellets, biomass and kerosene for one month.
insights.locator: Rapid emission growth from heavy industry continues

insights.claim: Indian industry has the second-lowest electrification rate in the G20, with the share of electricity in sectoral energy consumption lagging the world average in both level and rate of increase.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Industrial electrification is India's largest untapped decarbonisation lever and its biggest competitiveness gap versus peers.
insights.quote: Indian industry has the second-lowest electrification rate in the G20
insights.locator: Rapid emission growth from heavy industry continues

insights.claim: Unless the rate of industrial electrification picks up, further increases in Indian heavy-industry output will continue to translate directly into higher fossil-fuel consumption and CO2 emissions.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: India's emissions path is now a function of industrial policy, not power-sector policy — the key variable to watch.
insights.quote: Unless the rate of industrial electrification picks up, increases in heavy industry output will continue to translate into increases in fossil-fuel consumption and CO2 emissions.

themes.theme: Coal capital spending and lock-in risk

insights.claim: Generators added 8.5GW of new coal capacity over the two-year period even as fossil generation stagnated, leading to fewer running hours and increased costs for electricity consumers.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: New coal into a flat fossil-generation market means falling utilisation and stranded-cost pressure passed to ratepayers.
insights.quote: While fossil-fuel generation stagnated, generators added 8.5GW of new coal capacity, leading to fewer running hours and increased costs to electricity consumers.

insights.claim: Some 43GW of coal-power capacity was under construction in India at the end of June 2026, justified by the need to meet rising peak loads.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A 43GW pipeline entering a market where clean energy already covers all demand growth is the core stranded-asset question for Indian utilities.
insights.quote: Some 43GW of coal-power capacity was under construction at the end of June.

insights.claim: India is targeting capacity to process 100m tonnes of coal per year via coal gasification within four years for fertiliser and plastic feedstock, despite the technology still being nascent in the country with only Jindal Steel Limited operating it.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: An energy-security-driven push into an unproven, emissions-intensive technology at 100Mt scale is a large capital-misallocation risk.
insights.quote: The government is targeting a capacity to process 100m tonnes of coal per year in the next four years, despite the technology for coal gasification still being nascent in India.

insights.claim: India notified domestic coking coal as a 'critical and strategic mineral' in January 2026, and coal miners and steel companies are planning additional washeries to make it blendable with imported coal.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Strategic-mineral designation plus washery buildout signals sustained policy support for coal-based steelmaking, and potential import substitution for seaborne coking coal.
insights.quote: the government is aiming to increase the use of domestic coking coal, which it notified in January this year as a “critical and strategic mineral”

insights.claim: Continued Indian investments in coal gasification, domestic coking coal and new coal mining capacity could lock in coal use across industry for several decades.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: The power-sector plateau may prove temporary at the national level if industrial coal infrastructure is built out now.
insights.quote: These continued investments in coal gasification, domestic coking coal and new coal mining capacity could lock in coal use across industry for several decades.

insights.claim: India plans to cut average CO2 emissions per tonne of steel by 25% by 2025-26, mainly by reducing the share of coal-based steelmaking — a goal sitting in direct tension with its push to expand domestic coking coal supply.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Contradictory steel-sector policies mean stated intensity targets are weak guides to actual coal demand.
insights.quote: India plans to reduce its average CO2 emissions per tonne of steel by 25% by 2025-26, mainly by reducing the share of coal-based steelmaking.

insights.claim: Renewable power projects totalling 5.3GW missed completion deadlines and are paying penalties to the grid operator to retain network access.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence of execution slippage and financial penalty risk in India's renewables pipeline.
insights.quote: renewable power projects totalling 5.3GW missed completion deadlines and are having to pay penalties to the grid operator in order to retain network access

insights.claim: Curtailment has emerged as an issue in India particularly for projects relying on interstate power transmission, pointing to the need for network upgrades.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Curtailment directly erodes renewable project revenues and IRRs, especially for interstate-dependent assets.
insights.quote: Curtailment has emerged as an issue, particularly for projects relying on interstate power transmission, pointing to the need to upgrade the network.

insights.claim: India's flexibility plan for coal-power plants has been delayed by more than a year due to persistent regulatory bottlenecks, contributing to renewable-energy curtailment.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Regulatory delay on coal ramping is a direct, identifiable cause of wasted renewable output today.
insights.quote: A flexibility plan for coal-power plants has been delayed by more than a year due to persistent regulatory bottlenecks, contributing to the curtailment of renewable energy.

insights.claim: India's National Electricity Plan projected a requirement of 82GWh of energy storage capacity by 2026-27 rising to 411GWh by 2031-32.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Sets an explicit five-fold-plus policy target that frames the addressable Indian storage market this decade.
insights.quote: The National Electricity Plan projected a requirement of 82 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of energy storage capacity by 2026-27 and 411GWh by 2031-32.

insights.claim: As of May 2026 India had tendered around 272GWh of storage (142GWh pumped hydro, 133GWh batteries) against installed capacity of only 7.5GWh of batteries and about 60GWh of pumped hydro.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: The gap between tendered and installed storage implies a multi-year order book roughly 4x current fleet size for battery and pumped-hydro suppliers.
insights.quote: the government has issued tenders for around 272GWh of energy storage capacity, including 142GWh of pumped hydro and 133GWh of battery storage systems. Current capacity is 7.5GWh of battery storage and around 60GWh of pumped hydro.

insights.claim: The Central Electricity Authority has proposed that after June 2027 all new government-owned solar and wind projects carry mandatory two-hour battery storage, mirroring a policy China ran until scrapping it in early 2025 in favour of market-based approaches.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: A mandate would create step-change battery demand in India just as China abandons the same instrument — a notable policy divergence for cell manufacturers.
insights.quote: after June 2027, all new government-owned solar and wind projects would have “mandatory” two-hour battery storage

insights.claim: Expanding energy storage could reduce or eliminate the need to add thermal-power capacity to meet peak loads, undermining the main justification for new coal plants.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: If storage delivers, the 43GW coal pipeline risks becoming stranded peaking capacity rather than needed baseload.
insights.quote: Expanding energy storage has the potential to ease grid and flexibility constraints, while reducing or eliminating the need for adding thermal-power capacity to meet peak loads.

insights.claim: Coal-power emissions in this analysis are estimated by combining plant-level coal consumption from the Central Electricity Authority's monthly coal reports with station-specific calorific values and IPCC emission factors, splitting domestic from imported coal using a trailing two-month window of coal receipts.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: The headline flat-emissions result rests on plant-level official data rather than modelled proxies, strengthening its credibility.
insights.quote: Coal-power emissions are estimated by combining plant-level coal consumption from the Central Electricity Authority’s (CEA) monthly coal reports with data on the calorific value and emission factors of coal used at different power plants
